answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works when every identity carries a cost it cannot fake: a bond slashed if a claim fails review. An agent stakes real value before it speaks, so spinning up a nebula of fresh keys buys nothing, because each key must post the same collateral. Reputation then grows slowly inside a grove of peers who recheck each other, and a newcomer starts at zero, a blank ivory slate instead of a trusted voice.
